newsitem.title: INDIA: India parliament starts session in uproar.
newsitem.headline: India parliament starts session in uproar.

text.p: The monsoon session of India's parliament got off to a noisy start on Wednesday with both the upper and lower houses adjourned over lawmakers' demands for the dismissal of two regional governments.
Witnesses said government and opposition lawmakers engaged in angry shouting matches over a corruption scandal in the eastern state of Bihar and caste animosities in the western state of Maharashtra.

P.A. Sangma, the speaker of the lower house, or Lok Sabha, allowed a discussion in the house on Thursday on the Bihar situation and later on Maharashtra after adjourning Wednesday's proceedings until 2 p.m. (0830 GMT), officials said.
At one stage, Sangma threatened to resign if members did not cool down, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said. "You are demoralising the nation by your behaviour," he was quoted as saying.

Maharashtra has been rocked by tension between lower-caste Hindus, called Dalits, and upper-caste rivals since July 11 when a statue of socialist activist and Dalit leader B.R. Ambedkar was desecrated.
At least 12 people died when police opened fire on rioters in Maharashtra's capital city, Bombay.
The Lok Sabha resumed business at 2 p.m. when Home (Interior) Minister Indrajit Gupta made a statement on the Maharashtra tensions.

But deputies of the Congress party, which supports Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's centre-left United Front government, staged a walkout in protest against the statement, which they said was unsatisfactory.
The Congress has been seeking the dismissal of the regional Hindu Shiv Sena party government in Maharashtra, accusing it of failure in combating insults to Dalits.
"The act of desecration of the statue of Dr. Ambedkar and the subsequent police firing resulting in several deaths and injuries are extremely disturbing," Gupta's statement said.
"I have requested the chief minister to ensure that all relevant aspects of the case are thoroughly investigated and all culprits brought to book," he said.
Lawmakers of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) led the uproar against the government of Bihar, embroiled in a $280 million corruption scandal.

Bihar's chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, who has been indicted in the corruption scandal by federal police, says he will not resign from his post. He says he is innocent in the case, which involves alleged diversion of animal welfare funds.
Gujral's coalition is badly divided over its continuing association with a breakaway faction set up by Yadav early this month.
Coalition leaders are scheduled to debate the political deadlock on Friday.
